_comment: Instagram accounts the Instagram tab reads. HAND-CURATED. The tab has two halves and this file has four arrays. tier1/tier2 are DO — organisers, announcements, the caption is the event. see1/see2 are SEE — the people making content about this place, rendered as a photo wall. A handle's segment is WHICH ARRAY IT IS IN; there is no second map to keep in sync, so you move an account between halves by moving the string. The `1` arrays are fetched every run and the `2` arrays rotate, because each handle costs one Scrape Creators credit per run — that is refresh frequency, not importance, and it is independent of the segment. Drop a handle by deleting it; add one by appending. Nothing else may introduce a handle — the tab shows whoever is in here and nobody else. DO handles were vetted in the newsletter's reference/instagram-sources.md. SEE handles were vetted 2026-08-30 against the live Instagram profile API: every one exists, is public, and had posted within the preceding three weeks when it was added. Recency is a real criterion here — Burlington's meme and campus-confession pages are almost all dead (most last posted in 2021-2022) and a dormant account costs a credit a day to show nothing. A fifth array, `food`, is a TAG, not a roster: it names handles that already sit in one of the four arrays and belong to a kitchen, a bar, a market or someone who writes about eating here. Their posts carry f: 1 and fill the All Day Food tab’s “In their own words” rail. Listing a handle there costs nothing and fetches nothing; a handle that is only in `food` is ignored with a warning.

photo_categories._comment: TAGS for the Wire's Photos mode chips, like `food`: each array names handles that already sit in one of the four roster arrays. vibe: bars, cafes, breweries and venues whose posts show the room. pets: pet accounts. posters: accounts whose posts are event posters, on top of every DO (tier1/tier2) account, which the chip already counts. Food uses the `food` tag above plus all-day/data/food-directory.json. Hand-curated for now; build_instagram.py does not read this, so a later Instagram build can fill or replace it without touching the Wire.
